name: preflight-reminder
description: JIT reminder for AGENTS.md Rule 2 (Pre-Flight). Each user turn arms a flag; the first MUTATING tool call of the turn (write, edit, or a shell command that is not read-only) is blocked once with a Pre-Flight reminder, then everything is allowed. Read-only calls pass and keep the flag armed. A user reply that follows a hold, or a short approval reply (yes/go/ok/proceed...), option pick, or 2-3 word reply ending in one (fix + go; not no go), counts as approval (goose tells the model not to retry denials). Rule text is unchanged. 1.4.0: [[ / [ / seq and VAR=$(read-only cmd) classify as read-only; hold text states that goose's appended 'Do not retry' does not apply to a Pre-Flight hold. 1.5.0: named read-only scripts (resolve-target, pre-push-scan, verify-bundle, evaluate-alignment, status-kgm, status-fuseki) classify as read-only; redirects and other segments still checked. 1.6.0: agentfs-eval read-only scripts (template-check, agentfs-check, agentfs-behavior, runtime-compliance, static-sheet-status) and update-compliance.sh --check classify as read-only. 1.7.0: closes three bypasses (a mere mention of post-write.sh/checkpoint.sh exempted the whole command; command substitution in arguments or double quotes was not checked) — bookkeeping scripts are exempt only when run, $(..)/`..`/<(..) bodies are checked, $VAR script names resolved; redirects into /tmp are read-only; IS_RO_DEBUG=1; regression cases in tests/is-readonly-cases.sh. 1.8.0: one-pass quote tokenizer (a quote inside the other kind, escaped \" and $'..' no longer shift string boundaries — `echo "it's"; rm ...` passed before); sqlite3/awk scan only their own invocation (awk output/pipe to a string target and sqlite3 dot-commands count as changes); git check-ignore/check-attr/ls-tree/rev-list/merge-base/name-rev read-only, git branch <name> and reflog expire mutating; gsettings get/list, rpm -q/-V, secret-tool lookup/search, readelf/nm/objdump read-only. 1.9.0: a retry after a hold is recognised by the held call's saved tool response in sessions.db (tool_call_id), so a fast model's retry is not re-held as a batch sibling; the 2 s window is only the fallback.
